Split illustration of the three livestock management systems. Left: Extensive (cattle grazing freely in a large open savanna with a Fulani herdsman holding a stick). Middle: Semi-intensive (sheep in a fenced green paddock with a small wooden shelter in the background). Right: Intensive (pigs inside a fully enclosed, clean concrete pen with an automatic feeder and water nipple).

Routine piglet management tools. Three small panels. 1: A pair of pliers-like teeth clippers cutting the sharp needle teeth of a piglet. 2: A syringe administering an iron injection into a piglet's neck muscle. 3: A piglet's ear showing V-shaped notches for identification.

Poultry housing systems. Top: Deep litter system showing chickens freely walking on a floor covered with wood shavings, with round hanging plastic feeders and drinkers. Bottom: Battery cage system showing layers in tiered wire cages, with a long feed trough in front and a sloped floor where clean eggs have rolled out.

Proper rabbit handling and housing. Left: A person correctly holding a rabbit by grasping the scruff of its neck with one hand and supporting its rump with the other hand. Right: A wooden rabbit hutch raised on sturdy legs with a sloping roof, a wire-mesh front, and a wooden nest box inside.
